skill.name: analyse-google-ads
skill.description: Analyze Google Ads and Shopping performance through Product Metrics. Compare spend, conversions, and profit after ad costs, and investigate changes, stock risks, or product targeting. The CLI provides limited reporting. Reports do not edit Google Ads or store settings. Filing a requested proposal creates a separate record in Product Metrics.
skill.summary: Compare Google Ads performance, investigate changes, and flag unprofitable or stock-constrained products through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown tool names, routine Product Metrics reads, or documentation links. The CLI query fallback does not specify safe handling for dynamic SQL at the shell boundary. The skill also permits broader data reads and can file a requested proposal despite its blanket read-only description.

remediation.issue: Dynamic CLI query arguments have no safe execution guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Pass validated IDs and a single validated read-only query as separate process arguments, without shell interpolation. Prefer a structured reporting tool when available.

remediation.issue: Store selection can expand beyond the requested reporting scope.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to select stores before reading multiple properties. Confirm company-wide scope separately and do not present company totals as store totals.

remediation.issue: The read-only description omits proposal creation.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose proposal filing as a separate write action. Show the exact proposal and destination, then obtain explicit confirmation before creating the record.

The fixed Product Metrics CLI command lists stores for the connected account with no input interpolated.

content.user_title: Analyze Google Ads Performance and Profit
content.value_statement: Ad revenue alone does not show which campaigns are profitable or why performance changed. Product Metrics connects Google Ads results with store sales, margins, and inventory.
actual_capabilities: Compare account and campaign spend, conversion value, and ROAS across periods.
Investigate metric changes with campaign breakdowns, Ads change history, and store revenue.
Find search terms or products with spend but no reported conversions.
Report profit on ad spend by campaign or product, and flag stock risks.
Inspect product labels and targeting rules for Shopping campaigns and asset groups.
Use the CLI for store metrics, spend, break-even insights, inventory, and campaign plan results.
limitations: Detailed Google Ads reporting requires a connected Product Metrics MCP server and a linked Google Ads account.
The CLI does not provide detailed Google Ads reports, including search terms, keywords, or change history.
Recent conversions can arrive late. Search and Demand Gen profitability uses estimated margins.
Reports cover up to 400 days. Change explanations cover up to 90 days.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly Advertising Profit
use_cases.description: Compare ad spend and conversion value with the previous month. Identify campaigns below the store's profit threshold.

use_cases.title: Investigate a ROAS Drop
use_cases.description: Find which campaigns contributed to the drop. Check account changes, conversion delay, and the store's sales before drawing a conclusion.

use_cases.title: Find Advertised Products at Stock Risk
use_cases.description: Use profitability and inventory reports to identify advertised products at risk of running out.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Account Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize Google Ads for [store] over the last 30 complete days. Compare spend, conversion value, and ROAS with the previous period.

prompt_templates.title: Review Spend Without Conversions
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store], list search terms with at least [amount] in spend and no reported conversions over the last 30 complete days. Note recent conversion delays.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Performance Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain why Google Ads ROAS fell after [date] for [store]. Compare affected campaigns, account changes, conversion delay, and store revenue. Separate evidence from possible causes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Shopping Profit and Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store] and [date range], identify Shopping campaigns and products below break-even. Compare product segments and note stock risks. Check targeting rules for [asset group]. Label estimated margins and recommend checks without making changes.

output_examples.input: Example: Summarize May Google Ads performance for [store].
output: May spend was USD 4,000, up from USD 3,800 in April. Reported ROAS fell from 3.4 to 2.8.
Shopping generated USD 1,400 less conversion value. Its profit on ad spend was 0.9, below the store's break-even threshold of 1.0.

output_examples.input: Example: Explain the drop in reported conversions after June 10 for [store].
output: Google Ads reported 25% fewer conversions from June 11 to 17 than in the prior week. Store revenue was unchanged.
Conversion lag may explain part of the drop. Check for tracking changes before treating the drop as lost sales.

best_practices: Name the store and reporting dates, and confirm which stores to include before comparing several.
Check conversion lag before treating a recent decline as final.
Review profit on ad spend alongside ROAS and label any margin estimates.
anti_patterns: Treating high ROAS as proof of profit without checking margins.
Adding only the displayed rows and treating that sum as the account total.
Treating an account change that preceded a decline as proof that it caused the decline.

faq.question: What do I need for detailed Google Ads reporting?
faq.answer: Connect the Product Metrics MCP server and select a store with a linked Google Ads account. Some tools may require a Pro subscription.

faq.question: What can I do with only the Product Metrics CLI?
faq.answer: Review store metrics, ad spend, break-even insights, inventory, and plan results. Search terms, keyword reports, and Ads change history need MCP.

faq.question: How does POAS differ from ROAS?
faq.answer: ROAS divides conversion value by ad spend. POAS divides gross profit by ad spend and shows whether margin covers advertising costs.

faq.question: Which dates does the skill use by default?
faq.answer: It uses the last 30 complete days and compares them with the preceding period. You can request a different date range.

faq.question: Can it change my campaigns or store settings?
faq.answer: Reporting does not change Google Ads or store settings. If requested and permitted, the skill can file a separate proposal in Product Metrics for human approval.

faq.question: Are the latest conversion figures final?
faq.answer: No. Conversions can arrive after the initial report. The skill can check conversion lag before interpreting a recent decline.
